key_insight: A simple gradient-free Monte Carlo search can train deep neural networks by randomly mutating parameters and keeping changes only when loss improves, challenging the idea that backpropagation is necessary.
engineering_relevance: This suggests a practical alternative for training or adapting models when gradients are unstable, unavailable, or undesirable, including pruning, discrete weights, and unconventional activations.
method: Randomly perturb one parameter at a time
Accept the mutation if it reduces loss; otherwise retry
Use the same scheme to directly train deep or wide networks without backpropagation
evidence_signal: The abstract reports successful demonstrations on deep networks with more than 20 layers, wide single-hidden-layer networks up to 16,384 neurons, and a simple Transformer on MNIST and Tiny Shakespeare.
watch_item: The approach may be computationally inefficient due to repeated trial-and-error updates, so scaling and convergence cost are key implementation concerns.
paper_title: Beyond Backpropagation: Monte Carlo Method Can Train Deep Neural Networks
